title: Quantum Corridor, Ciena, and Toshiba Validate 1.6 Tb/s Quantum-Safe Encryption on Live Fiber Network - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantum Corridor, Ciena, and Toshiba field-trialed 1.6 Tb/s of live commercial fiber traffic secured simultaneously by NIST PQC and QKD between Chicago and Hammond, Indiana, showing legacy 800G optical hardware can be software-upgraded to PQC without hardware replacement and that QKD channels can coexist with classical traffic on a single fiber pair without dark fiber.

themes.theme: Live network validation of hybrid quantum-safe encryption

insights.claim: Quantum Corridor, Ciena, and Toshiba completed a field trial validating 1.6 Tb/s of encrypted optical capacity secured simultaneously by post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) on Quantum Corridor's live production fiber network connecting Chicago, Illinois, and Hammond, Indiana.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: First reported instance of dual-layer (mathematical + physics-based) quantum-safe defense running live on commercial infrastructure at 1.6 Tb/s scale, a concrete proof point for enterprises and carriers evaluating PQC/QKD deployment timelines.
insights.quote: the trial validated 1.6 Terabits per second (Tb/s) of encrypted optical capacity secured simultaneously by post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).
insights.locator: Midwest network infrastructure developer Quantum Corridor

insights.claim: The trial used Ciena's Waveserver platform with WaveLogic 6 Extreme (WL6e) coherent optics running NIST-certified post-quantum cryptographic algorithms alongside Toshiba's QKD servers, which continuously fed quantum-generated symmetric key material directly into Ciena's optical encryption system, delivering wire-speed AES-256-GCM encryption at the optical layer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Names the specific vendor stack (Ciena WL6e + Toshiba QKD) investors should track as the reference architecture for carrier-grade quantum-safe optical networking deals going forward.
insights.quote: The field deployment utilized Ciena's Waveserver platform powered by WaveLogic 6 Extreme (WL6e) coherent optics to deliver wire-speed, optical-layer AES-256-GCM encryption.
insights.locator: The field deployment utilized Ciena's Waveserver

insights.claim: Legacy WaveLogic 5 Extreme (WL5e) 800G encrypted traffic ran alongside the new PQC/QKD trial over the same RLS photonic line system, demonstrating that existing 800G optical links can be upgraded to support PQC algorithms via software without replacing physical line hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A software-only upgrade path to PQC on already-deployed 800G hardware sharply lowers the capex and migration friction for carriers, implying faster, cheaper PQC rollout across existing fiber networks than a hardware refresh cycle would require.
insights.quote: demonstrating that legacy 800G optical links can be upgraded to support PQC algorithms via software without replacing physical line hardware.
insights.locator: The trial operated alongside existing WaveLogic 5 Extreme

insights.claim: Company commentary frames the trial as the first time a 1.6 Tb/s live channel has been secured simultaneously with both PQC (mathematical defense) and QKD (physics-based defense), explicitly positioned as neutralizing 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks where adversaries store intercepted data today to decrypt once cryptographically relevant quantum computers exist.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense-in-depth (PQC+QKD together) is being marketed as the gold-standard response to HNDL risk, a framing investors should expect competitors (e.g., other QKD/PQC vendors) to adopt or counter in positioning.
insights.quote: The trial represents the first time a 1.6 Tb/s live channel has been secured simultaneously with both PQC (mathematical defense) and QKD (physics-based defense), neutralizing “harvest now, decrypt later” threats

insights.claim: The deployment validated Toshiba's photonic multiplexing capability enabling Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) QKD channels and classical data traffic to coexist over a single fiber pair, removing the requirement for dedicated dark fiber infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Eliminating the dark-fiber requirement materially cuts deployment cost and expands the addressable base of carriers who can adopt QKD using existing lit fiber, a key adoption unlock for Toshiba's QKD business.
insights.quote: The deployment successfully validated Toshiba's photonic multiplexing capability, enabling Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) QKD channels and classical data traffic to coexist over a single fiber pair without requiring dedicated dark fiber infrastructure.

insights.claim: By embedding encryption directly into the optical transport layer via compact modules on the Waveserver platform, enterprises can achieve compliance with government quantum-safe mandates (including U.S. and France's ANSSI requirements) through simple software upgrades, avoiding the cost and complexity of replacing thousands of edge routers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions optical-layer PQC as a lower-cost compliance path versus router-level replacement, relevant to enterprises and government contractors budgeting for PQC migration mandates in the U.S. and France.
insights.quote: enterprises can achieve compliance with government mandates—such as those from the U.S. and France's ANSSI—through simple software upgrades, avoiding the massive cost and complexity of replacing thousands of edge routers.

insights.claim: Quantum Corridor is scaling its planned 263-mile fiber network, as a member of the Bloch Tech Hub and Chicago Quantum Exchange ecosystem, to serve research universities, defense contractors, financial institutions, and AI workloads requiring high-bandwidth, quantum-resistant data transmission.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 263-mile regional quantum-safe fiber buildout targeting defense, finance, and AI-workload customers signals a concrete near-term commercial expansion path and customer base to watch for follow-on contracts.
insights.quote: Quantum Corridor is scaling its planned 263-mile fiber network to serve research universities, defense contractors, financial institutions, and AI workloads requiring high-bandwidth, quantum-resistant data transmission.
insights.locator: As a member of the Bloch Tech Hub
